reply.title: Squashing with a Sigmoid Curve
reply.story: When modeling probabilities or neural activations, we often need to convert any real number into a bounded range between zero and one. A linear scale fails because it grows infinitely, but a sigmoid curve bends gracefully as inputs grow large. Pierre François Verhulst first studied this logistic growth to describe population limits, where resources constrain exponential expansion. The resulting S-shaped curve acts as a smooth switch, mapping infinite inputs into a strict interval. By adjusting the steepness and the central midpoint, we control how sharply this transition occurs.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic function squashes infinite inputs into a bounded range between 0 and 1. Adjust steepness and midpoint to see the S-curve change.
reply.instructions: Move the sliders to change steepness and midpoint. Observe how the curve bends and the tangent slope updates at the marker.
